name: Nordic functional outdoor
summary: The plain, tough dress of the Nordic hike and the long trek. A wax-proofed twill jacket, wool and fleece layers, and a design that serves the trail first.

philosophy.core_thesis: Dress for a day out in all weather. Simple shapes, tough cloth that can be waxed and mended, and layers that serve the walker for a lifetime.
design_principles: Weave a dense poly-cotton twill of 300 to 400 g per square metre for the jacket and the trouser.
Rub in wax each season to keep the cloth proof against rain and wind.
Cut the jacket roomy, for 3 layers of wool and fleece beneath.
Add a large chest pocket and a hood that fits over a cap.
Reinforce the knee, the seat and the elbow with a second layer.
Choose a muted earth colour that sits in forest and fell.
Repair a worn piece in place with a patch, not with a new buy.
anti_patterns: A glossy, thin shell for the city
Bright colour that clashes with the fell
A tight cut that blocks layers
A throwaway piece with no repair path

silhouette.shape: A roomy anorak or jacket with a large chest pocket and a hood, over wide trousers with reinforced knees and a boot cut.
silhouette.line: A straight shoulder, a plain, boxy body to the hip and a hem with a drawcord.
silhouette.fit: Loose enough to carry fleece and wool beneath; the drawcord and the cuff close out the wind.
silhouette.proportion: Jacket to the hip; trouser rise of 28 cm; roughly 1 to 1.1 chest to hip.
rules: Put one large pocket on the chest of the anorak.
Reinforce the knee and the seat of the trouser with a double layer.
Add a hood that closes with a drawcord and fits over a cap.
Use a drawcord at the hem and an elastic cuff.
Keep the colour muted: green, grey, sand and wool white.

fabrics.rule: Choose a dense, windproof cotton and polyester twill that takes wax, with wool and fleece beneath: the cloth must be waxed and mended for years.

methods: double layer at knee and seat
large chest pocket on the anorak
construction.closures: A half zip or a full zip with a storm flap, a drawcord at the hood and the hem, and a hook-and-loop cuff.
construction.details: A large chest pocket, a double-layer knee and seat, a long back for the pack, and a patch of the same cloth on each elbow.

surface.pattern: Plain colour; a nordic pattern on a wool jumper.
surface.gloss: The waxed twill at 5–15 GU; fleece at 1–3 GU.
surface.wear: The wax wears at the crease and the owner rubs in a new coat; the cloth darkens and the patches show years of use.

palette.strategy: Earth tones that sit in forest and fell: green, sand, grey and wool white, with one signal colour on the pack.

processes: wax impregnation by hand and by machine
cutting and sewing in a small factory
patching and repair by the owner
design for repair in the pattern
making.scale: Made in small firms in Norway and Sweden for the home market, then sold to walkers across the world.
making.signs: A waxed twill with a dark patina, a large chest pocket, a double-layer knee, and a muted earth colour.

pieces.form: Pullover anorak with a large chest pocket and a drawcord hood
Wide trouser with a double knee and seat
Waxed canvas parka with a deep hood
Plain fleece jacket for the mid layer

evidence.title: Jacket of the G-1000 range with woven label

emotion.target_response: A calm, honest sense of being at home in the cold and the forest: simple, durable and without show.

use_cases: a product brief for a repairable outdoor jacket
an image prompt for a Nordic trail scene
a costume brief for a 1970s trek
a study note on durable dress
avoid_when: the brief is glossy, technical alpine wear

modifiers.how: Swap the waxed twill for a laminated membrane, tape the seams and thin the cut.
Add a down-filled, baffled jacket as the mid layer, and keep the waxed shell.

ornament_level.note: The jacket is plain; a Nordic pattern appears only on a wool jumper.
